title: Citizen science: new tools & data
sub: Symposium topic 10 · Silvertown 2009 vs Fraisl et al. 2022
blurb: From 'new dawn' to 'new standard': GBIF, eBird, the Ten Principles and Haklay's participation levels.
h1: From new dawn to new standard: citizen science in ecology
lede: Group 10's topic. Classic: Silvertown (2009), 'A new dawn for citizen science'. Recent: Fraisl et al. (2022), citizen science in environmental and ecological sciences.
six: **Citizen science**: members of the public take part in real research, mostly by contributing observations.
Volunteer data are biased (easy places and times, a few heavy contributors), so **filter for quality** and **model the observation process** (effort, occupancy–detection).
**eBird** collects bird checklists with effort data; **GBIF** aggregates occurrence records. Volunteers supply 50 %+ of GBIF data.
**Ten Principles of Citizen Science** (ECSA, 2015): good practice from genuine science outcomes to feedback, open data, credit and ethics.
**Haklay's levels**: 1 crowdsourcing → 2 distributed intelligence → 3 participatory science → 4 extreme citizen science.
Silvertown: modern citizen science is open to all, not a privileged few. Fraisl: it is now a standard method, with quality control and ethics built in.
foot: Source: Group 10 symposium slides and study guide; glossary section 10.

questions.q: Why must citizen-science data be analysed carefully?
questions.answer: They are biased toward easy places and times
questions.e: Filter for quality and model the observation process.

questions.answer: Bird observations with explicit effort (start time, duration)
questions.e: Complete checklists with bounded effort are best.

questions.answer: Aggregates occurrence records and sampling-event datasets
questions.e: Volunteers supply over 50 % of GBIF data.

questions.q: Haklay's Level 1, where volunteers only collect data, is…
At which level do citizens co-design questions, methods, analysis and use of results?
How does Haklay's typology differ from Arnstein's ladder?
questions.answer: Every Haklay level has value; Arnstein runs from bad to good
questions.e: Haklay's levels are flexible and people can move between them.

questions.q: Who wrote the Ten Principles of Citizen Science?
questions.e: Written 2013–2015, for good practice, a framework and credibility.

questions.q: Which principle is served by newsletters telling volunteers what came of their data?
The Christmas Bird Count started in…
questions.e: Proposed by ornithologist Frank Chapman instead of the Christmas 'side hunt'.

questions.q: What separates modern citizen science from its historical form, according to Silvertown?
questions.answer: It is potentially available to all, not just a privileged few
questions.e: His three drivers: technology, the public as a free resource, funders demanding outreach.

questions.answer: QA happens before and during collection; QC happens after
wrong: QC is only for satellite data
questions.e: QA: training, protocols. QC: flagging outliers, checking photos.

Four levels of participation from crowdsourcing to extreme citizen science.
